analysis.title: 2027 Investment Outlook: Under Pressure: Questions Shaping the Next Market Cycle
key_insights: Allspring frames 2027 as a year of wide outcomes from geopolitical shocks, shifting rate expectations and the scale of AI investment. It argues portfolio resilience matters more than getting one market forecast right.

Ron Insana (independent commentator, compensated by Allspring, views his own) names geopolitical risk as his biggest concern. He worries that separate flashpoints could compound into a shock with oil, trade and risk repricing hitting together, leaving central banks facing weaker growth and higher inflation.

Insana says the speed of interest rate moves matters more than the level. An abrupt repricing of rate expectations, with heavy government and corporate refinancing and issuance, would pressure long yields, stock valuations and earnings.

Insana sees AI as transformational but following the historical pattern of technologies that attracted excess capital and later corrections. He calls AI financing increasingly complex and dubious, and says AI is vulnerable to higher rates because of the capital it needs.

Allspring's Scheiber says the stock/bond diversification relationship is less dependable because inflation is more persistent and volatile. He recommends adding commodities, real return strategies and active currency strategies beyond stocks and bonds.

Allspring fixed income (Wise) says 2026 showed markets and economies adapt to shocks, and prefers a flexible, opportunistic approach over one large macro call. The team is adding agency MBS after weakness, finding opportunities in CMBS and reducing parts of ABS.

Allspring systematic equity (Campbell) treats macro as a risk management problem, modelling company sensitivities to growth, inflation, rates, credit spreads and commodities. It expects the market to be less forgiving of concentrated bets in 2027.

Scheiber wants broad AI exposure through semiconductors, electricity demand, power infrastructure, industrial production and commodities, split between enablers and adopters. He says to separate revenue growth from economic profit and check financing sustainability.

Campbell expects 2027 to hinge on evidence of return on AI capex and sees the opportunity broadening to power, cooling and connectivity bottleneck solvers. He watches for net equity issuance turning positive, AI IPO demand and post-lockup insider selling as bubble signals.

Shimada (EM equity) favors early AI adopters in emerging markets and says the EM AI theme is more attractive and less risky than in developed markets, citing valuations. The chart shows the EM AI Big 10 trading at a 60% or better forward P/E discount to the Magnificent 7 through 2028.
Insana is concerned about sequencing: financing bills may come due before evidence that AI spending produces real returns, as in the internet boom.

Wise's base case is a midcycle adjustment with growth resilient enough for a few more Fed hikes without recession. He sees the larger risk at the long end in that case, and more front-end pressure if inflation stays sticky and hiking is protracted. He calls the belly of the curve the sweet spot in both scenarios.

Wise says investors can lean into higher yields without reaching for spread and add a little duration in the middle of the curve. Over 40 years, when the Bloomberg US Aggregate yielded above 3%, its 3-year forward return was positive 100% of the time.
Scheiber says bonds could deliver attractive returns in a slowdown if inflation falls with growth. If growth weakens while inflation stays high, the outcome is less favorable.

Venditti (munis) now prefers bonds around 15 years over the 20-year area he liked a year ago. He sees comparable yield with less duration and maturity risk, and limited compensation for stretching further.

Insana is cautious on extending duration. He says that with sticky inflation and firm nominal growth the Fed could be behind the curve, and long yields could rise sharply before policy slows the economy.

Campbell says US large-cap concentration is historically high and past high-concentration periods were followed by better relative returns from small caps and equal weight. The Russell 2500 trades at 17.5x forward P/E against 19.0x for the S&P 500, a 0.92x relative ratio versus a 1.16x 25-year median.

Shimada says Taiwanese and Korean earnings estimates rose about 40% from the start of 2026, and expects Taiwan and Korea to keep 20%-plus earnings growth in 2027 while China and India accelerate to the mid-to-high teens. She also likes copper and metals and mining on supply constraints.

Wise says fixed income concentration can rise as the largest borrowers issue more debt, with AI financing as the current example. He says broadening can occur as investors find better compensation elsewhere without large issuers stumbling.

Insana notes concentration preceded major bear markets in 1929, 1968 and 1999. He recommends rebalancing, protecting gains and checking that winners have not grown too large, especially for shorter-horizon investors.
Campbell advises looking down the cap spectrum and outside the US, citing cheaper SMID valuations and accelerating earnings, but says cheaper does not automatically mean better.

Shimada says China growth is near 5%, property prices have bottomed and stimulus is increasing, with consumer and real estate equities in deep-value territory. She also names ignored Andean and ASEAN markets and agricultural and soft-commodity exporters as opportunities.

Scheiber describes emerging markets as more diversified than 20 to 25 years ago. He names India and Southeast Asia as beneficiaries of supply chain rebuilding, Mexico as a connector country, and Brazil for high real rates with lower government debt.

Venditti prefers A+ and higher-rated munis, vanilla general obligation and essential-service revenue bonds, because credit risk is expensive. He says after-tax yields compare well with private credit without its liquidity constraints.

Insana says global diversification is a weaker case than a year ago, especially where currency moves erode overseas returns. He prefers high-quality munis and short Treasuries and is cautious on private credit liquidity terms and financing risks in a rising-rate environment.
Insana says protection is still relatively cheap and calls this a great time to rebalance.

sector_views.sector: Technology / AI infrastructure (semiconductors, power, cooling, connectivity)
sector_views.rationale: Scheiber and Campbell want exposure to AI enablers, with Campbell favoring bottleneck solvers in power, cooling and connectivity. Both stress separating revenue growth from economic profit.
Campbell says the Russell 2500 trades at 0.92x the S&P 500 forward P/E against a 1.16x median while earnings accelerate.
Shimada expects earnings to broaden beyond Taiwan and Korea to China and India, with valuations below historical averages.
Shimada cites supply constraints and secular demand supporting copper.
Venditti favors A+ and higher-rated GO and essential-service bonds around 15 years for yield with less duration risk.
Insana is cautious on liquidity terms and financing risks in a rising-rate environment.

earnings_insights: Shimada: Taiwanese and Korean earnings estimates have risen roughly 40% since the start of 2026, and she expects 20%-plus earnings growth from both in 2027 (forecast).
Shimada: China and India earnings growth could accelerate into the mid-to-high teens in 2027 (forecast).
Campbell: earnings began accelerating down the cap spectrum and outside the US in 2026.

macro_indicators.reading: A few additional Fed hikes in the base case
macro_indicators.interpretation: Wise expects growth to be resilient enough to absorb a few more hikes without recession, with more risk at the long end.

macro_indicators.indicator: Bloomberg US Aggregate Bond Index yield to worst
macro_indicators.interpretation: Higher starting yield improves the fixed income return outlook.
Shimada says property prices have bottomed and stimulus is increasing.
A discount to the S&P 500 at 19.0x forward P/E, a 0.92x ratio against a 1.16x median.

trade_ideas.description: Add duration in the middle of the US yield curve (belly)
trade_ideas.rationale: The belly is the sweet spot in both the midcycle-hike and sticky-inflation scenarios.
trade_ideas.risk: Long-end yields could rise on a midcycle adjustment, and front-end pressure builds if inflation stays sticky.

trade_ideas.description: Shift municipal exposure from 20-year to about 15-year maturities, favoring A+ and higher-rated GO and essential-service bonds
trade_ideas.rationale: Comparable yields with less duration and maturity risk.

trade_ideas.description: Tilt equities toward small and mid-caps and international markets
trade_ideas.rationale: Valuations are cheaper and earnings growth is accelerating outside US large caps.
trade_ideas.risk: Cheaper does not automatically mean better, so stock selection matters.

trade_ideas.description: Add emerging market AI adopters and copper/metals and mining exposure
trade_ideas.rationale: EM AI Big 10 trade at a 60% or better forward P/E discount to the Magnificent 7, and copper has supply constraints.

trade_ideas.description: Rebalance concentrated equity positions, hold more liquidity and buy relatively cheap protection
trade_ideas.rationale: Insana says risks are hard to time and protection is cheap.

risk_factors: Geopolitical risks compounding into a shock to oil, trade and supply chains, leaving central banks facing weaker growth and higher inflation.
An abrupt repricing of interest rate expectations from reaccelerating inflation or a policy misjudgment.
Heavy global government and corporate refinancing and issuance pressuring long yields.
AI financing risk: heavy borrowing and optimistic return assumptions that financing bills may come due before returns are proven.
Equity concentration in US mega-caps tied to a single theme.
Less reliable stock/bond diversification under persistent inflation.
Private credit liquidity terms and financing risks in a rising-rate environment.

vol_and_positioning: Insana says protection is still relatively cheap.
Campbell says stock-level dispersion has been very high, favorable for stock selection.
Campbell cites net equity issuance turning positive as a classic bubble indicator and watches AI IPO demand and insider behavior after lockup expirations.
geopolitical: Insana names geopolitical risk as his biggest 2027 concern, with flashpoints that could compound.
Iran conflict settled into an uneasy stalemate in 2026.
Tariffs were imposed and then pulled back.
China sharply reduced oil imports while supply was disrupted.
Venditti notes municipal bonds are insulated from geopolitical risk such as Iran.

tension_points.bull_case: Scheiber and Campbell see AI as a productivity revolution with broadening opportunity in power, cooling and connectivity. Shimada says EM AI is cheaper, with a 60% or better forward P/E discount to the Magnificent 7.
tension_points.bear_case: Insana says financing bills may come due before evidence of real returns, as in the internet boom, and that financing is increasingly complex and dubious.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Disappointment in AI financing conditions or expected profitability, or net equity issuance turning positive.

tension_points.bull_case: Wise says to add duration in the belly of the curve, since higher starting yields improve returns and the Aggregate's 3-year forward return was positive every time yields exceeded 3%.
tension_points.bear_case: Insana is cautious on extending duration, since sticky inflation could leave the Fed behind the curve and long yields could spike.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Inflation reaccelerating or policymakers misjudging the growth and inflation balance, causing an abrupt repricing of rate expectations.

tension_points.bull_case: Campbell and Shimada expect leadership to broaden to small caps, international and EM as earnings accelerate and valuations are lower, without needing mega-caps to break.
tension_points.bear_case: Insana cites concentration before the 1929, 1968 and 1999 bear markets and urges rebalancing and protecting gains.

tension_points.bull_case: Campbell, Shimada and Scheiber favor international and emerging markets, citing better earnings growth and supply chain shifts.
tension_points.bear_case: Insana is more selective than a year ago, since currency moves can erode overseas returns, and prefers high-quality munis and short Treasuries.

theme_stances.evidence: The conditions are there for leadership to broaden.

theme_stances.evidence: The belly of the curve is the sweet spot across both scenarios.
